title: Setting your hourly rate and minimum charge for bond and end-of-lease cleaning
audience: Owners of bond and end-of-lease cleaning businesses who need a base hourly rate, a per-job check and a minimum charge before they quote.
learningOutcomes: Separate billable hours from non-billable hours, and calculate the time available to bill.
Calculate a base hourly rate from the owner's own costs and income target, then compare it with local evidence.
Set a minimum charge for short jobs, and explain it to a client before the visit.

instruction.heading: What moves the rate for move-outs
instruction.body: The rate depends on the crew's skill and reliability, how much a dirty or hard-to-clean move-out takes, how quickly you can deliver to an agent's deadline, and the cost of running the business. Bond cleaning is usually sold per job, so the hourly rate is a tool for building the job price, not a price to advertise. The research did not find an Australian hourly rate or a per-move-out price set for bond cleaning. Use your own costs first, then compare with local evidence.

instruction.heading: Counting the hours that can be billed
instruction.body: Paid hours include travel, quoting, site visits, admin, marketing, training, equipment care, sick days and leave, which are not billable. Jobber's general guide puts billable time at about 60 to 80 per cent of working hours. That is not an Australian figure. If you can bill 60 of every 100 paid hours, the costs of all 100 must come from the 60, so the rate is about 1.67 times the rate for a fully billable week (CALC).

instruction.heading: Building the rate from costs and income
instruction.body: Add the annual running costs (insurance, vehicle, equipment and its upkeep, phone, software, marketing and accounting) to the income you need, including leave and super where you pay wages. Business.gov.au says on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure (1 October 2026). Divide the total by billable hours. Business Victoria advises including total overheads and reviewing prices about every three months (no date shown).

instruction.heading: Use the minimum charge for site visits and short jobs
instruction.body: A site visit to quote a move-out costs travel and time even if no job follows. Contractor+ suggests setting a minimum from the full visit cost, divided by one minus the target margin, and states that the minimum should cover travel, set-up and cleanup. Its figures are labelled illustrative and are not used here. Gap: the research did not find an Australian minimum or call-out charge for bond cleaning. State any visit fee in writing before the visit.

instruction.heading: Check the rate against the proxy band and review it
instruction.body: Compare the rate with the proxy band for move-outs, which is $160 to $220 for a two-bedroom home (Beyond Pricing, 28 October 2026). That is short-stay fee data, so it is a sense check and cannot set the rate. Review the rate each quarter and record any change and its reason.

procedure: Estimate the paid working hours in a year, then subtract travel, visits, admin, marketing, training and leave to find billable hours.
List the annual running costs, including insurance, vehicle, equipment, products, phone, software and marketing.
Add the income needed, with leave and tax allowances confirmed by a registered tax agent.
Divide the total by billable hours to find the base rate.
Set a visit fee or minimum charge that covers travel and set-up, and state it in writing before any visit.
Check the base rate against the proxy band and local evidence, then review it each quarter.

workedExamples.situation: [ILLUSTRATIVE] A solo bond cleaner plans for about 1,800 paid hours a year and expects to bill 60 per cent of them. Annual costs and the income needed total $66,000 (illustrative). A site visit costs about $60 in travel and time (illustrative).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What base rate is needed, what does a typical move-out earn at that rate, and what visit fee should apply?
workedExamples.reasoning: Billable hours are 1,800 x 0.60, which is 1,080 (CALC). The base rate is $66,000 divided by 1,080, which is $61.11 an hour. A move-out timed at 6.5 hours would earn $397.22 at that rate (CALC), which is far above the proxy band of $160 to $220 for a two-bedroom home (Beyond Pricing, 28 October 2026). The gap shows that the band cannot set the price: the move-out price must follow the hours and scope. The visit fee follows the Contractor+ method: $60 divided by 0.70 is $85.71 at a 30 per cent target margin (illustrative figures).

commonErrors.error: Setting the rate from a short-stay fee table.
commonErrors.prevention: Build the rate from your costs and billable hours. Use the table as a sense check only.

commonErrors.error: Pricing as though every paid hour could be billed.
commonErrors.prevention: Subtract visits, admin, marketing, travel and leave before you divide.

commonErrors.error: Doing unpaid site visits with no visit fee stated.
commonErrors.prevention: State the visit fee in writing before the visit.

commonErrors.error: Assuming Jobber's 60 to 80 per cent range applies in Australia.
commonErrors.prevention: Use your own log of paid and billable hours for a month.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Price display: show the total price including GST (business.gov.au, 18 January 2024). The research did not confirm the rules for minimum or call-out charges, so check current ACCC guidance before you publish a visit fee.
Where you employ cleaners, the Cleaning Services Award may set their pay: Level 1 adult minimum of $25.85 an hour with 25 per cent casual loading from 1 July 2025. The 2026-27 rates were not checked.
Tax treatment of leave and super for a sole trader was not confirmed. Check it with a registered tax agent before the rate is published.
This lesson does not grant a cleaning licence or insurance. Licence rules for bond cleaning were not researched, so check the rules for the state where the work is done.

qualityStandard: Billable hours are calculated from a logged or estimated month, not assumed.
The base rate is built from the owner's costs and income target, and is compared with local evidence.
A minimum charge is set and stated before any short job.
documentationEvidence: Annual costs and income worksheet, with the source and date of each cost
Billable hours calculation showing the non-billable deductions
Price sheet showing the base rate, the minimum charge and the review date
summary: Price a move-out from billable hours, not paid hours, then check the job price against your costs.
The short-stay proxy band is a sense check. It cannot set the rate.
Gaps: no Australian bond hourly rate, per-job price or minimum visit fee was found in the research.

knowledgeChecks.question: A bond cleaner can bill 60 of every 100 paid hours. How should the rate be built?
options: From all paid hours, so the rate looks lower
From billable hours, so costs and income come from the work that can be billed
From the short-stay fee band for two-bedroom homes
From the rate the owner would like the market to pay

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a site visit to quote a move-out have a stated fee?
options: Travel and set-up time do not shrink with a small job or a cancelled visit
Clients expect every visit to cost the same
A visit fee replaces a written quote for the job
Visits need no set-up time at all

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the right use of the Beyond Pricing move-out band?
options: A bond price to quote straight from
A sense check, labelled as a short-stay proxy
A legal minimum for every job
A substitute for your own costs and hours

sourceReferences: business.gov.au, 'Choose a pricing strategy', https://business.gov.au/products-and-services/choose-a-pricing-strategy, page metadata dated 1 October 2026. Supports: on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure.

Jobber Academy, 'What are billable hours', https://getjobber.com/academy/what-are-billable-hours/, published 5 November 2024, last modified 20 July 2026. Supports: billable time is about 60 to 80 per cent of working hours; a general range, not an Australian figure.

Business Victoria, 'Develop a pricing strategy', https://business.vic.gov.au/business-information/finance/pricing-for-profit/develop-a-pricing-strategy, no date shown. Victoria. Supports: include total overheads and sales costs in the price; review prices about every three months.

Contractor+, 'Minimum Service Call Charge: A Contractor's Pricing Guide', https://contractorplus.app/blog/minimum-service-call-charge, 23 September 2026. Supports: a minimum can be set from the full visit cost divided by one minus the target margin, and should cover travel, set-up and cleanup. The page labels its figures illustrative; none are used here.

Beyond Pricing, 'Short-term rental cleaning fees (Australia)', https://beyondpricing.com/au/blog/how-much-should-you-charge-for-cleaning-fees-in-your-australian-holiday-rental, dated 28 October 2026. Vendor source; short-stay fee data. Supports: per-turnover bands by property size; move-in and move-out bands by bedroom count; a $120 per-turnover illustration; city labour benchmarks; fixed rates suit smaller properties and hourly rates suit larger or luxury homes.
business.gov.au, 'Display prices', https://business.gov.au/legal/fair-trading/display-prices, page metadata 18 January 2024. Supports: displayed prices should show the total price, including GST.

Fair Work Commission, Cleaning Services Award (MA000022), https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000022.html, variation effective 1 July 2025. Supports: Level 1 adult minimum hourly rate of $25.85 and a 25 per cent casual loading. The 1 July 2026 position was not checked.
Notes: 1,800 paid hours, the $66,000 target, the $60 visit cost, the 6.5-hour move-out and the 30 per cent margin are illustrative. The $160 to $220 band is a short-stay proxy.
